question: What evidence supports the occurrence of oxidative abiotic dechlorination of trichloroethene under aerobic conditions?
answer: The generation of formic/glyoxylic acid and glycolic/acetic acid in trichloroethene (TCE)-amended sediments under aerobic conditions provides direct evidence of oxidative abiotic dechlorination. These organic acids (OAs) were either absent or present at lower levels in non-TCE controls, confirming TCE degradation. Although only a small fraction of TCE was transformed (e.g., 0.04 in sediment 1), the increasing OA trends over time indicate ongoing dechlorination. No CO₂ production above background levels was observed, consistent with prior studies suggesting minimal CO₂ release under sustained TCE concentrations. These findings align with previous observations of aerobic oxidative dechlorination pathways.
